question: Which Indian Mass Movement began with the famous 'Dandi March' of Mahatma Gandhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Civil Disobedience Movement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Civil Disobedience Movement began with Mahatma Gandhi's famous "Dandi March" (Salt Satyagraha). (सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन — दांडी मार्च)

• Gandhiji started the march on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) with 78 followers and reached Dandi (a coastal village in Gujarat) on 6 April 1930, where he broke the salt law by making salt from sea water.

• The march covered about 240 miles (about 385 km) in 24 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) was launched after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Khilafat issue; it was withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident (February 1922).

• Option 3 — the Quit India Movement began on 8 August 1942 in Bombay with the slogan "Do or Die".

• Option 4 — the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) in Gujarat was a peasant movement against revenue collection during crop failure.

NOTE

• The Civil Disobedience Movement led to the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (March 1931), after which Gandhiji attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931) in London.

• Gandhiji's first satyagraha in India was the Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar, on behalf of indigo cultivators.

question: Whose autobiography is titled 'An Unsuitable Boy'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karan Johar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "An Unsuitable Boy" is the autobiography of the Indian film director and producer Karan Johar, co-written with Poonam Saxena and published in 2017. (करण जौहर की आत्मकथा)

• The title is a playful reference to Vikram Seth's celebrated novel "A Suitable Boy".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Karan Johar heads the production house Dharma Productions (founded by his father Yash Johar) and directed films such as Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, My Name Is Khan and Ae Dil Hai Mushkil.

• Aditya Chopra heads Yash Raj Films; Hansal Mehta directed Shahid and Aligarh; Sanjay Kapoor is an actor-producer.

NOTE

• Famous Indian autobiographies/memoirs:

◦ Wings of Fire — A. P. J. Abdul Kalam; My Experiments with Truth — Mahatma Gandhi.

◦ Playing It My Way — Sachin Tendulkar; Ace Against Odds — Sania Mirza.

◦ An Era of Darkness — Shashi Tharoor; Romancing with Life — Dev Anand.

question: The length of the men's kabaddi court is _____ metres.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• For men (seniors), the kabaddi court measures 13 metres in length × 10 metres in width. (पुरुष कबड्डी कोर्ट — 13 मीटर लंबा)

• For women (seniors), the court is 12 metres × 8 metres.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kabaddi is played between two teams of 7 players each (with 5 substitutes); a match consists of two halves of 20 minutes with a 5-minute break.

• Key terms: raider, anti-raider (defender), cant (chanting "kabaddi"), lobby, bonus line, baulk line, lona (all-out bonus of 2 points).

NOTE

• Kabaddi is the state game of Tamil Nadu; India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and the Asian Games (kabaddi was introduced there in 1990).

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) was launched in 2014 and popularised the sport nationally.

question: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Zoya factor'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anuja Chauhan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Zoya Factor" (2008) is a best-selling novel written by the Indian author and former advertising professional Anuja Chauhan. (अनुजा चौहान)

• The story revolves around an advertising executive, Zoya Singh Solanki, who is believed to be a lucky charm for the Indian cricket team; it was adapted into a 2019 film starring Sonam Kapoor and Dulquer Salmaan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Anuja Chauhan's other novels: Battle for Bittora, Those Pricey Thakur Girls, The House That BJ Built and Baaz.

• Kiran Desai won the Man Booker Prize (2006) for "The Inheritance of Loss".

• Sudha Murty wrote "Wise and Otherwise", "Mahashweta" and "Three Thousand Stitches"; she is also known for her philanthropy through the Infosys Foundation.

• Nandini Bajpai is an Indian-American author of young-adult fiction such as "A Match Made in Mehendi".

NOTE

• Indian Booker connections: Arundhati Roy — The God of Small Things (1997); Kiran Desai — The Inheritance of Loss (2006); Aravind Adiga — The White Tiger (2008); Geetanjali Shree — Tomb of Sand (International Booker, 2022).

question: Who among the following has NOT received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2021 (given in February 2023) for his/her contribution in dance ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sumitra Guha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sumitra Guha did NOT receive the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2021 in the field of dance — she is a distinguished Hindustani classical vocalist (Carnatic-trained singer of the Kirana gharana style), honoured in the field of music, not dance. (सुमित्रा गुहा — संगीत, नृत्य नहीं)

• The other three names are all dancers who were among the awardees announced/conferred in February 2023 for the year 2021:

◦ Neena Prasad — a celebrated Mohiniyattam exponent from Kerala.

◦ Jayalakshmi Eshwar — a noted Bharatanatyam dancer and guru.

◦ Thokchom Ibemubi Devi — a distinguished Manipuri dance exponent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama; its headquarters is in New Delhi.

• It confers the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) and the even higher Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) — the fellowships are restricted to 40 living persons at a time.

• The awards for 2019, 2020 and 2021 were presented together by the President of India at a ceremony in 2023.

NOTE

• India's three national academies: Sangeet Natak Akademi (performing arts), Sahitya Akademi (literature) and Lalit Kala Akademi (fine arts) — all set up in the early 1950s.

• The eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle based on the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi?
option_1: To promote industrialisation in urban areas
option_3: To prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health
option_4: To promote cottage industries in rural areas
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote industrialisation in urban areas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To promote industrialisation in urban areas" is NOT a Gandhian Directive Principle. Gandhian philosophy stressed village self-sufficiency, decentralisation and cottage industries, not large-scale urban industrialisation. (गांधीवादी सिद्धांत नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Gandhian Directive Principles in Part IV of the Constitution include:

◦ Article 40 — to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

◦ Article 43 — to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas.

◦ Article 43B — to promote co-operative societies (added by the 97th Amendment, 2011).

◦ Article 46 — to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and other weaker sections.

◦ Article 47 — to prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health.

◦ Article 48 — to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle.

NOTE

• Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36–51) are contained in Part IV, borrowed from the Irish Constitution. They are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

• DPSPs are classified into Socialistic, Gandhian and Liberal–Intellectual principles.

question: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total incomes earned by individuals and businesses in an economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Income method.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Income method" calculates national income by adding up all the incomes earned by the factors of production — rent (land), wages/salaries (labour), interest (capital) and profit (entrepreneurship) — by individuals and businesses in an economy during a year. (आय विधि)

• By this method: National Income (NNP at factor cost) = Rent + Wages + Interest + Profit + Mixed income of the self-employed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Value-added / Product (Output) method — national income is found by adding the value added by every producing unit in each sector (primary, secondary, tertiary), avoiding double counting.

• Expenditure method — national income is found by adding all final expenditure: GDP = C + I + G + (X – M), i.e., private consumption + investment + government expenditure + net exports.

• All three methods, if correctly applied, give the same national income.

NOTE

• Key aggregates: GDP, GNP (= GDP + net factor income from abroad), NNP (= GNP – depreciation); NNP at factor cost = National Income.

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The first scientific estimate was by Dadabhai Naoroji ("Poverty and Un-British Rule in India").

question: What is personal income?
option_1: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
option_2: The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
option_3: The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
option_4: The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions
solution_text:
The correct answer is The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Personal income" is the total income actually received by individuals and households from all sources before the payment of direct taxes and other deductions. (व्यक्तिगत आय — करों से पहले)

• Formula: Personal Income = National Income – Undistributed corporate profits – Corporate tax – Net interest paid by households – Social security contributions + Transfer payments.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes "Personal Disposable Income" — the income left after paying direct taxes:

◦ Disposable Income = Personal Income – Direct (personal) taxes – Miscellaneous fees/fines.

◦ Disposable income is divided into consumption and saving.

• Option 2 describes corporate/business income (corporate profit), not personal income.

• Option 3 describes mixed income of the self-employed, which is only one component of personal income.

NOTE

• Sequence of income concepts: National Income → Private Income → Personal Income → Disposable Income.

• Per capita income = National Income ÷ Total population — used as a rough measure of the standard of living.

question: Who founded the Hindu reform organisation Brahmo Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta in 1828 (initially as the Brahmo Sabha). (ब्रह्म समाज — राजा राम मोहन राय, 1828)

• It preached monotheism (worship of one formless God) and opposed idol worship, casteism, polytheism, sati and child marriage.

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" and the "Maker of Modern India"; his efforts led Lord William Bentinck to abolish sati in 1829 (Regulation XVII).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ramkrishna Paramhans was the spiritual guru of Swami Vivekananda, who founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897) at Belur Math.

• Debendranath Tagore (father of Rabindranath Tagore) revived the Brahmo Samaj in 1843; Keshab Chandra Sen later led a splinter group (Brahmo Samaj of India, 1866).

• Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867.

NOTE

• Other reform movements: Arya Samaj — Swami Dayanand Saraswati (1875, Bombay), slogan "Back to the Vedas"; Theosophical Society — Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott (1875, New York; Indian HQ at Adyar, Madras); Satyashodhak Samaj — Jyotiba Phule (1873).

question: Whom among the following Indian singers is known as 'Gazal King'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jagjit Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jagjit Singh (1941–2011) is popularly known as the "Ghazal King" (also "Ghazal Samrat") for popularising the ghazal among ordinary Indian listeners by simplifying its classical presentation. (ग़ज़ल सम्राट — जगजीत सिंह)

• He was born in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, and was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2003.

• Famous ghazals/albums: "Hothon Se Chhu Lo Tum", "Tum Itna Jo Muskura Rahe Ho", "Jhuki Jhuki Si Nazar", and the album "The Unforgettables" with his wife Chitra Singh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Manna Dey was a legendary playback singer (Dadasaheb Phalke Award, 2007) famous for classical-based songs like "Laga Chunari Mein Daag".

• Mukesh was known for his melancholic voice and songs picturised on Raj Kapoor.

• Shailendra was a celebrated lyricist (not a singer), known for songs in Raj Kapoor's films.

NOTE

• A ghazal is a poetic form of Persian/Urdu origin made of couplets (shers) sharing a rhyme (radif/qafia).

• Other great ghazal singers: Mehdi Hassan ("Shahenshah-e-Ghazal"), Begum Akhtar ("Mallika-e-Ghazal"), Ghulam Ali, Pankaj Udhas, Talat Aziz.

question: Dree Utsav is celebrated in the state of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Dree Festival (Dree Utsav)" is an agricultural festival celebrated by the Apatani tribe of the Ziro Valley in Arunachal Pradesh, usually on 5 July every year. (ड्री उत्सव — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

• Prayers and sacrifices are offered to the gods Tamu, Metii, Medvr and Danyi for a bumper harvest and to keep away famine, pests and epidemics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Arunachal Pradesh: Losar (Monpa New Year), Solung (Adi tribe), Nyokum (Nyishi tribe), Mopin (Galo tribe), Reh (Idu Mishmi), Boori Boot (Hill Miri) and Siang River Festival.

• The Apatani cultural landscape of the Ziro Valley is on UNESCO's tentative list for its unique wet-rice cultivation without draught animals.

NOTE

• Festivals of neighbouring states: Bihu (Assam), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland), Wangala (Meghalaya, Garo tribe), Sangai Festival (Manipur), Chapchar Kut (Mizoram) and Kharchi Puja (Tripura).

question: ___________ word of Indian dance is derived from a Sanskrit word and literally means 'taking towards'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abhinaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abhinaya" comes from the Sanskrit roots "abhi" (towards) + "ni/naya" (to lead/carry), literally meaning "taking/leading towards" — that is, carrying the sentiment of the performance towards the spectator. It refers to the expressive, dramatic aspect of Indian classical dance. (अभिनय)

• According to the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni, Abhinaya is of four kinds:

◦ Angika — expression through body and limbs.

◦ Vachika — expression through speech, song and recitation.

◦ Aharya — expression through costume, ornaments and make-up.

◦ Sattvika — expression of genuine emotion and psychological states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Nritta" — pure dance, i.e., rhythmic movement of the body without expressing any meaning or emotion.

• "Nritya" — a combination of Nritta and Abhinaya, i.e., dance with expression and meaning.

• "Taandava" — the vigorous, masculine and energetic aspect of dance, associated with Lord Shiva.

• "Laasya" — the graceful, gentle and feminine aspect of dance, associated with Goddess Parvati.

NOTE

• The Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharat Muni (c. 200 BCE–200 CE), is the foundational treatise on Indian dance, drama and music; it is often called the "fifth Veda".

question: Which of the following is an example of the Western Coast Port?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai Port.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mumbai Port (in Maharashtra) lies on the western coast of India, on the Arabian Sea. It is a natural harbour and was historically the largest port of India. (मुंबई बंदरगाह — पश्चिमी तट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Major ports on the WESTERN coast (Arabian Sea): Kandla/Deendayal (Gujarat), Mumbai (Maharashtra), Jawaharlal Nehru Port–Nhava Sheva (Maharashtra), Mormugao (Goa), New Mangalore (Karnataka) and Kochi (Kerala).

• Major ports on the EASTERN coast (Bay of Bengal): Kolkata–Haldia (West Bengal), Paradip (Odisha), Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Kamarajar–Ennore, Chennai and V. O. Chidambaranar–Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu).

• Port Blair (Andaman & Nicobar Islands) is the 13th major port.

NOTE

• Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), Nhava Sheva, is India's largest container-handling port; Kandla (Deendayal Port) is a tidal port; Visakhapatnam is India's deepest natural port; Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hooghly.

question: What are the three tiers of the Government in India?
option_1: Union government, Judiciary government and Federal government
option_2: Union government, State Government and Federal Government
option_3: Union government, State government and Judiciary government
option_4: Union Government, State Government and Local Government
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Government, State Government and Local Government.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has a three-tier system of government: (भारत में सरकार के तीन स्तर)

◦ Union (Central) Government — for the whole country, based in New Delhi.

◦ State Governments — for each of the States.

◦ Local Governments — Panchayati Raj Institutions in rural areas and Municipalities in urban areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The third tier (local self-government) was given constitutional status by the 73rd Amendment (1992) for Panchayats and the 74th Amendment (1992) for Municipalities, both effective from 1993.

• Panchayati Raj has three levels: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block/intermediate) and Zila Parishad (district).

• Rajasthan was the first state to implement Panchayati Raj (2 October 1959, Nagaur), followed by Andhra Pradesh.

NOTE

• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system; the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a two-tier system.

• The Judiciary is an organ of the state (along with the Legislature and the Executive), not a tier of government — which is why Options 1 and 3 are wrong; "Federal Government" is simply another name for the Union Government, so Option 2 is redundant.

question: The foundation of Sanchi Stupa was laid by which of the following Kings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashoka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi (in Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh) was originally commissioned/founded by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. (सांची स्तूप — सम्राट अशोक)

• Ashoka built it as a brick stupa over the relics of the Buddha; it was later enlarged with stone casing, railings and the famous carved toranas (gateways) during the Shunga and Satavahana periods.

• Sanchi was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A stupa is a hemispherical Buddhist funerary mound; its parts are the anda (dome), harmika, chhatra (umbrella), medhi and pradakshina path.

• Ashoka (r. c. 268–232 BCE) embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and spread the Dhamma through rock and pillar edicts; his Lion Capital at Sarnath is India's State Emblem.

• The Sanchi Stupa appears on the reverse of the Indian ₹200 currency note.

NOTE

• Bimbisara and Chandragupta Maurya were earlier rulers (Haryanka and Maurya dynasties); Samudragupta was a Gupta ruler of the 4th century CE, praised in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) by Harisena.

question: During which months do retreating monsoons occur in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is October and November.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Retreating Monsoon" (also called the post-monsoon or "October Heat" season) occurs in India during October and November, when the south-west monsoon winds withdraw from the subcontinent. (लौटता हुआ मानसून — अक्टूबर–नवंबर)

• During this period the low-pressure trough over North India weakens and is gradually replaced by a high-pressure system; the monsoon retreats from north-west India by early October and from the peninsula by early December.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The retreating monsoon brings rainfall to the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu and coastal Andhra Pradesh) through the north-east monsoon, which picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

• Tropical cyclones frequently strike the eastern coast during this season.

• The four seasons recognised by the IMD: Cold weather (December–February), Hot weather (March–May), South-West Monsoon (June–September) and Retreating Monsoon/Post-monsoon (October–November).

NOTE

• The south-west monsoon normally reaches Kerala around 1 June and covers the whole country by mid-July. Mawsynram/Cherrapunji in Meghalaya receive the highest rainfall in India.

question: Which is the primary structural component responsible for most of the mechanical strength of the cell wall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cellulose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cellulose" is the primary structural component of the plant cell wall and provides most of its mechanical strength and rigidity. (कोशिका भित्ति — सेलुलोज)

• It is a polysaccharide made of long unbranched chains of β-D-glucose units joined by β-1,4-glycosidic bonds; these chains group into microfibrils that give great tensile strength.

• Cellulose is the most abundant organic compound on Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chitin forms the cell wall of fungi and the exoskeleton of arthropods (insects, crabs) — it is not the main component of the plant cell wall.

• Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide of animals and fungi, stored mainly in the liver and muscles.

• Heparin is an anticoagulant (it prevents blood clotting) secreted by basophils and mast cells; it has no structural role in cell walls.

NOTE

• The plant cell wall also contains hemicellulose, pectin and lignin (lignin adds hardness to wood).

• Humans cannot digest cellulose (they lack the enzyme cellulase); it acts as dietary fibre/roughage. Ruminants digest it with the help of gut micro-organisms.

question: Ball and spring model of chemical bonds obey:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hooke's law.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the "ball and spring model" of chemical bonds, atoms are treated as balls (masses) and the bonds between them as springs. Such a vibrating bond behaves like a simple harmonic oscillator and therefore obeys Hooke's law. (हुक का नियम)

• Hooke's law states that, within the elastic limit, the restoring force is directly proportional to the displacement: F = –kx, where k is the force constant (here, the bond's stiffness).

• A stronger bond has a larger force constant and vibrates at a higher frequency — the principle behind infrared (IR) spectroscopy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Charles' law — at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (V ∝ T).

• Newton's law of gravitation — every mass attracts every other mass with a force F = Gm₁m₂/r².

• Newton's laws of motion — inertia; F = ma; action and reaction.

NOTE

• Hooke's law was given by Robert Hooke (1660); the SI unit of the force constant k is N/m.

• The elastic limit is the point beyond which a body does not regain its original shape; Young's modulus measures the stiffness of a material.

question: Pandit Janki Prasad was associated with which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banaras.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Janki Prasad was the founder/originator of the Banaras (Varanasi) gharana of Kathak. (बनारस घराना — पंडित जानकी प्रसाद)

• The Banaras gharana is distinguished by its natural body movements (swabhavik chaal), the use of the "thaat" and equal footwork on both sides of the stage, and by the bols invented by Janki Prasad himself.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The three principal gharanas of Kathak are:

◦ Lucknow gharana — founded by Ishwari Prasad; developed under Thakur Prasad and Bindadin Maharaj/Kalka Prasad; famous for bhava (expression) and grace. Modern exponent: Pandit Birju Maharaj.

◦ Jaipur gharana — founded by Bhanuji; known for strong, fast footwork (tatkar) and layakari (rhythmic play).

◦ Banaras gharana — founded by Janki Prasad.

• The Raigarh gharana (Chhattisgarh) was developed under the patronage of Raja Chakradhar Singh.

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), derived from the word "katha" (story) — performed by "kathakars" (story-tellers).

• Famous Kathak exponents: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan, Gopi Krishna and Kumudini Lakhia.

question: In 2023, Ajay Singh, the chief of SpiceJet was appointed as president of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ASSOCHAM.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2023, Ajay Singh, the Chairman and Managing Director of SpiceJet, was appointed/elected as the President of ASSOCHAM — The Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India. (एसोचैम अध्यक्ष — अजय सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• ASSOCHAM, founded in 1920, is one of India's oldest apex chambers of commerce; its headquarters is in New Delhi. Its tagline is "Knowledge Architects of Bharat".

• FICCI (Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry) was established in 1927 by G. D. Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas; HQ New Delhi.

• CII (Confederation of Indian Industry) was founded in 1895; HQ New Delhi.

• NASSCOM (National Association of Software and Service Companies) was founded in 1988; it is the apex body of the IT–BPM industry.

NOTE

• SpiceJet is a low-cost Indian airline; Ajay Singh revived it after taking control in 2015.

• These industry bodies act as a bridge between industry and the government on policy matters.

question: Rohit Sharma became the first ever Indian to play how many T20 cricket matches in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 400.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2022, during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in Australia, Rohit Sharma became the first-ever Indian cricketer to play 400 T20 matches (counting internationals, the IPL and other domestic/franchise T20 competitions). (रोहित शर्मा — 400 टी20 मैच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rohit Sharma, nicknamed "Hitman", holds the record for the highest individual score in ODIs — 264 (against Sri Lanka at Eden Gardens, 2014) and is the only batter with three ODI double-centuries.

• He has led Mumbai Indians to five IPL titles and captained India to the ICC T20 World Cup title in 2024.

• He was also the first batter to score five T20I centuries.

NOTE

• T20 cricket was introduced in England in 2003; the first T20 World Cup (2007) in South Africa was won by India under M. S. Dhoni.

• The IPL began in 2008.

question: Which form of Indian dance is said to be 'soft and suitable for female presentation'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Laasya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Laasya" is the soft, graceful, gentle and delicate aspect of Indian dance, traditionally described as suitable for female presentation. (लास्य — कोमल, स्त्री-सुलभ नृत्य)

• It is associated with Goddess Parvati, who is said to have performed it in response to Shiva's vigorous Tandava.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Taandava" is the vigorous, forceful and masculine aspect of dance, associated with Lord Shiva in his form as Nataraja (Lord of Dance).

• "Nritta" is pure dance — rhythmic body movement with no expression of meaning.

• "Nritya" is Nritta combined with Abhinaya — dance that conveys emotion and meaning.

NOTE

• Natya = drama/dance-drama combining Nritta, Nritya and Abhinaya, as classified in the Natya Shastra.

• The dance forms of India are classified as classical (8 forms) and folk (Garba, Bhangra, Bihu, Ghoomar, Lavani, Dandiya, etc.).

question: Which of the following oceans is surrounded by the continent of North America and South America to the east?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pacific Ocean has North America and South America lying on its eastern side (i.e., the Americas bound the Pacific to the east), while Asia and Australia lie to its west. (प्रशांत महासागर)

• The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean in the world, covering about one-third of the Earth's surface; the deepest point on Earth, the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep, about 11,000 m), lies in it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest ocean; the Americas lie to its west and Europe/Africa to its east. It is famous for the S-shape and for the Gulf Stream current.

• The Indian Ocean is the third largest and the only ocean named after a country; it is bounded by Asia (north), Africa (west) and Australia (east).

• The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest, located around the North Pole.

NOTE

• The "Ring of Fire" — a horseshoe-shaped belt of volcanoes and earthquake zones — surrounds the Pacific Ocean.

• Ocean order by size: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern (Antarctic) > Arctic.

question: The famous 'Pashupatinath Temple' is located in which country from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "Pashupatinath Temple" is located on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Nepal. (पशुपतिनाथ मंदिर — नेपाल)

• Dedicated to Lord Shiva as "Pashupati" (Lord of all living beings), it is one of the holiest Hindu shrines and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979.

• The present pagoda-style temple was built in the 17th century by King Bhupatindra Malla, though the site is far older.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Nepal: capital Kathmandu, currency Nepalese Rupee; the world's highest peak Mount Everest (Sagarmatha, 8,848.86 m) lies on the Nepal–China border.

• Bhutan: capital Thimphu, currency Ngultrum; famous for the Tiger's Nest (Paro Taktsang) monastery and the concept of Gross National Happiness.

• Maldives: capital Malé, currency Rufiyaa. Sri Lanka: capitals Colombo (commercial) and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (legislative); famous for the Temple of the Tooth (Kandy).

NOTE

• Nepal shares borders with five Indian states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim.

• Only devotees of Hindu faith (from the Indian subcontinent) are permitted inside the main sanctum of Pashupatinath.

question: In which of the following years was the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first (inaugural) Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav — a National Tribal Sports Meet — was held in 2023, at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar (Odisha). (प्रथम जनजातीय खेल महोत्सव — 2023)

• It was organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs with the Sports Authority of India and Odisha government, to identify and nurture sporting talent from tribal communities across the country.

• Thousands of tribal athletes from across India competed in disciplines such as athletics, archery, football, kabaddi, kho-kho, volleyball and tug of war.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 15 November is celebrated as "Janjatiya Gaurav Divas" (Tribal Pride Day) — the birth anniversary of the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda; it was first observed in 2021.

• Other related initiatives: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS), TRIFED and the "Van Dhan Yojana" for tribal livelihoods.

NOTE

• Major national sports events in India: Khelo India Youth Games (since 2018), Khelo India University Games, Khelo India Winter Games and the National Games.

• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was created in 1999; tribal welfare is safeguarded under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution.
